claim: The attribute is wrapped in `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK`, so it is never emitted for projects targeting netstandard2.0 or .NET Framework. Those are the targets the generator is commonly used on. `System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute` exists on both: it has been in System.dll since .NET Framework 2.0 and is in the netstandard2.0 surface, and on those targets it is valid on classes. So the guard is not needed for compilation, and generated code on these targets is still not excluded from coverage. This misses the acceptance criterion 'All generated code is decorated with ExcludeFromCodeCoverage'. The derived criterion only asks for conditional emission where the attribute does not exist, which does not apply here. The same guard is repeated in every template: FormatterTemplate, StringKeyFormatterTemplate, EnumTemplate, UnionTemplate, ResolverTemplate and CompositeResolverTemplate.
